First round was most crucial. Past work experience was relevant and I could come up with suggestions from my experience. I tried to tell them  that I know about the M&A process and concepts like TSA, due diligence, integration, separation, SLA, Day 0, Day 1, Day 2. This gave him an idea that I have a basic understanding of M&A and IT part of it. He was noting them down in his laptop. Further  during case I tried to cover my answer following MECE approach and kept taking his feedback about whether I need to  cover any other aspect. It helped me as in some situations he said I have almost covered all points and sometimes he helped me to consider some points that I missed. I wrote every point and detail he provided in a structured way as he was looking and reading them all. Clarifying case situations and asking  for feedback at every analysis helped. In one or two situations he was not convinced with some points, instead of neglecting them I tried giving logical reasons behind them and he seemed to like that. Also asking a relevant question to him at the end of the interview was important. He was very much willing to answer.

Mock Sales (in CPO round) - Sell IIM Indore as a service. I did not understand the question carefully, and thought of trying to sell an IIM Indore service that can be taken up by Tech Mahindra. Went with TCS Ion, and gave them solutions and kept speaking for 1-2 mins. One of the panelists then mentioned that I have not really understood the question and asked the questioner to repeat. Only when he repeated - I clarified the understanding with him and then took a minute to answer. My answer was the Jigsaw Academy IIM Indore course can be taken over or sold to TechMahindra. I was the salesperson for IIM Indore (the organisation) trying to sell the online analytics course of IIM Indore to TechM (the client). Gave basic details about the course, pros and cons in the sense - no extra work needed to be done, as the videos were already recorded by IIM Indore faculty and this is a MOOC course(did not use this term in the interview and kept it very simple and in layman terms). Said that the only expense will be in evaluation for the participants in the MOOC which can be outsourced back to IIM Indore or we can hire other evaluators. Follow up questions  - We (TechM) already have a Learning & Development System, why should we buy from IIM Indore. I answered with a clarifying question - who teaches are they academia or industry experts. Very tough answer - said academics that move to industry. Used a different pivot saying that IIM Indore researches in all fields and industries and has experts from various fields are in the institute. So, since TechM is working and looking for clients across the domains and industries, this acquisition/collaboration can help. Final question - Why should they (client) not go with IIM Ahmedabad and go with IIM Indore? I answered that there are obvious differences since IIMA was set up in the 60s and IIMI in 1997, however, the student & faculty body is large and diverse and even being a younger institute the quality of our research is top notch etc etc. 
- Note: Be jovial, happy and do not let the nervousness show even when it's a stress interview. Confidence is the key. And keep going at it, attack the problem from multiple POVs. In situational question, following the case method helps, but do it sparingly, this was not a case interview and the interviews went along only for 20 mins, so there are only so many questions you can ask. In this case, clarifying the initial question / case should have been done, and understanding the exact question they are asking (in this case which service or what type of product of IIM Indore to sell) would have wasted less time.

Case-based Questions:
1) Paytm has started a referral system to increase its customer base. How can we make this system viral?
Approach: Started by asking preliminary questions like what the referral system is, how it works, objective of launching it, the geography that we want to target etc. Then moved on to divide the present customer base into several segments based on age, income and usage of the app. Finally, suggested various marketing techniques that can be employed for each of the customer segment.
Tip: Be aware of various digital marketing techniques.
2) The no. of subscribers in the Paytm mutual funds segment have decreased in last few years. How would you go about it?
Approach: Asked questions on what the business is, types of customers, types of subscriptions, trends in the last few years in each type of subscription. Also, shed some light on overall economy and mutual fund business as a whole. The interviewer asked me to stop in between, hence, no recommendations were given.
Tip: Ask as many questions as you can in a structured manner to understand the root cause of the problem. Don't jump to the recommendation part directly.

"Why Paytm?" was asked in the 1st interview.
Approach: Spoke about the various business segments within Paytm, the segment that I am more interested in and the sense of entrepreneurship (freedom/ownership) that can be obtained to work for a business which is in its nascent phase and at the same time being backed by the huge brand name of the organization.
Tip: Know well about the company.

1) Why was PPO not being offered by the organization that you interned in? Did you under-perform? Did you reject the PPO?
Approach: Told all the good things about the organization and the project. Told him honestly that I have no clue as to why PPO wasn't offered.
Tip: Don't make any negative remarks on your past organization.
2) You interned in a fin role, your resume is more tilted towards fin, then why did you apply for this role (S&M)? Do you know where your interests lie?
Approach: Said that I don't have a specific domain interest. Just like to play with numbers. We are here to understand business as a whole.
3) What electives have you taken in 2nd year? (Asked questions on luxury retail management)
Tip: Name a few electives from every domain.

We had a huge problem as time was less and people were many. Having the position of the moderator was a huge advantage as you will get a sure shot chance at speaking minimum two times, once at the start and other at the end.
The opener was the one who got the most peaceful time, as anyone who followed had trouble in making points as for about 20 secs minimum of 3 people will be talking simultaneously. I spoke in only 4 of the 5 times. In the last 2 cases, I had to fight my way to speak a minimum 2 times each which allowed me to go forward. Overall it was a fish market and no one focussed on the overall case objective given to all of us.
- Tips:
1. Focus on the objective of the Case and it was very clearly reminded by the HR at the end of the cases. That can really help in moving forward.
2. In a GD with so many people don't try to counter anyone as it will waste your precious time.
3. When multiple people talk, DO NOT STOP speaking, as at one point people will stop. This helped me as I was speaking only random words for the last 2 cases as the people simultaneously talked. I was saying the phrase "Negative PR for the Company" and "Expansion by B2B2C" continuously till everyone stopped speaking, this allowed me to make my point started the moment people stopped. ( A trick which can only work on Online mode)
4. BE ON POINT and DO NOT GLOBE
5. Fancy words are good, but it is better to have your points in a language as simple as possible. Ultimately you have to deal with normal consumers and hence your speaking skill will matter and need to accommodate common people
6. The number of times you speak does matter as ultimately you want them to notice you!

In interview 1, I was asked to estimate the customer lifetime value of a fitness center. I asked him whether I have to estimate for any specific brand or in general. he told me any would do. I told him I was a member of cult.fit and therefore would like to estimate the lifetime value for it. I analyzed it for 3 customer profiles - the fitness freak, a person who would continue for 1-2 years and a person who would just take a membership once and never renew. Based in this, I calculated lifetime values for each of them and then took the average. He was happy with my approach, but suggested I could have taken the route of churn rates as well (I used very few technical terms).
In the second question, he asked me to guess the average revenue of any Starbucks outlet in Delhi. I told we can calculate it as avg cost of one order * no of orders. He was satisfied with this and then I told that the average cost of an order can be taken as Rs 200. Then, to calculate average no of orders, I told for Starbucks, the takeaway orders would be limited, so we'll consider only the dine-in orders. For no of dine-in orders, I considered the operating hours, capacity, average occupancy and no of people/seat in an hour. I took some time to arrive at this number, though I kept interacting with him about this approach. He told me I could have taken a guess for no of orders instead of calculating it this way. He then asked me to guestimate the number of outlets of Starbucks that should be opened in Delhi. I told him we can consider area of Delhi and then base our calculation on it. He told that instead we should look into population density as in Delhi sometimes two Starbucks are present in one road, based on the population density of the locality.

Case Based GD. For us, the GD was about a car rental company that sought to expand their profits. We were also asked to comment about the existing business model and suggest improvements. We were given multiple data points and facts but were only allowed a limited amount of time to read the case (5 mins approx) after which we were thrown headfirst into the GD. It is advisable to start making notes IMMEDIATELY after the case is viewed.
- As for tips, I am genuinely not an expert xD, but it's always a good idea to: 
- 1) identify constraints, parameters and important variables
2) identify why the aforementioned variables and constraints are not optimal
3) brainstorm ideas to bring it to optimal levels through the GD
- I also paid heed to the advice given by our seniors and tried to be one of the first two-three speakers. I went in second and established the context - the constraints, the parameters and the important variables - and therefore lent a structure to the GD. I would not hesitate to recommend the same approach - be one of the first to speak.

Case Based GD. For us, the GD was about a quick commerce start-up which has recently started selling luxury perfume on its platform. However, the sales of this product aren't good enough compared to the industry average of other quick commerce companies selling the same product. We were required to discuss the pros and cons of selling the luxury perfume on the quick commerce platform and come up with recommendations on how the start-up can increase the sales of this luxury perfume. We were given multiple data points and facts but were only allowed a limited amount of time to read the case (5 mins approx) after which we were thrown headfirst into the GD. It is advisable to start making notes IMMEDIATELY after the case is viewed. 
- As for tips, I am genuinely not an expert xD, but it's always a good idea to: 
- 1) identify constraints, parameters and important variables
2) identify why the aforementioned variables and constraints are not optimal. You may use one of the frameworks to do so if it fits however don't try to force fit it. 
3) brainstorm ideas to bring it to optimal levels through the GD
- I started the GD and contributed around 5 times within the given 12 minute timeframe. I made a conscious effort to take notes during the GD, helping me keep track of the discussion's direction and the topics that were covered.

1-Chairman GD: 8 candidates, 8 rounds, with each candidate being the chairman in one of the rounds.
2. Each round will have a case-based GD, mostly on a company scenario:
Theme of cases asked to our panel: declining profits, new market exploration, ad campaigns for a new or existing product, conflict management, and organization restructuring.
